data.narrative:
Epsilon3, a Series A-stage space and aerospace company founded by Laura Crabtree and Max Mednik, has raised $19M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 6 public peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private counterparts including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and ICEYE, though the private set spans multiple stages and thus limited direct comparability.

Of three potential valuation methods, only stage-progression proves applicable. The peer-median approach fails due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting quality thresholds—while 14 same-sector peers exist, none yielded three or more datapoints in tight filters. Public-comp anchoring is inapplicable absent disclosed revenue; the Space & Aerospace public median trades at 26.4x P/S across the five identified tickers, but cannot be applied without the target's top-line figures. Stage-progression, applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier from the $19M total raised proxy, yields $38M.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $32M to $44M, centered on $38M, derived from a single defensible method. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable private-company transaction data at Epsilon3's stage, undisclosed revenue preventing public-comp calibration, and the inherent volatility of early-stage space ventures. This narrow methodological base warrants conservative use of the range and close attention to subsequent funding signals and revenue trajectory.
